liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **High Time** (1 review): Listener calls High Time real sweet and a highlight, noting an interesting slide solo from Bob [28]
- **Crazy Fingers** (1 review): Listener describes Crazy Fingers, Uncle John's, and Playin' In The Band as real sweet [24]
- **Maggie's Farm** (1 review): Listener notes Maggie's Farm rocks, but wished for the other song after it per Bob's direction [25]
- Listener considers the Playing in the Band performance an overlooked gem [26]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-09-19.126346.mtx-redo.eichorn.sbeok.t-flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 135 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1987-09-19.126284.mtx.eichorn.sbeok.t-flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 135 min; rated 1/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1987-09-19.137413.sbd.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 135 min; rated 1/5 by 1 [6]
- **gd1987-09-19.sbd.painoman.76469.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 137 min; rated 2.75/5 by 4 [8]
- **gd1987-09-19.176816.senn441.lamarre.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 135 min [11]
- **gd1987-09-19.nak300.pasternak.mallick.105569.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 136 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [14]. Said about its sound: Listener notes lots of bandwidth retained and bright levels, hearing the Garden in its resonant glory [30]
- **gd1987-09-19.nak300.damico.90485.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 134 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [15]. Said about its sound: Listener notes very good recording quality with extremely minor distortion present [26]
- **gd1987-09-19.nakcm304.suraci.82419.flac16**: source not stated; 19 songs; 131 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [18]. Said about its sound: Listener rates the sound as high quality grade A with a perfect mix of crowd and music; Listener rates the sound quality at 4 out of 5 stars [24][25]

## Around the show

- Listener attended their second show, noting the Farm Aid comments were strange at the time [23]
- Listener recalls bringing their mother and father to this specific show [26]
- Listener notes Dead Heads in 1987 disliked Black Peter and Around & Around as downers [27]
- Listener states Miracle, Maggie's Farm, and Black Peter were part of the Farm Aid III TV broadcast [27]
- Listener describes the venue as filled with the same energy as the night before [30]
- Uploader notes Maggie's Farm was broadcast on TV for Farm Aid [6]
- Listener compares the show to the previous night's monster Dew, calling this one outstanding playing [28]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-09-19.126346.mtx-redo.eichorn.sbeok.t-flac16**: transferred by Roger Eichorn; source: Another Matrix from Source 1: SBD (shnid=76469) SBD>CD>EAC>FLAC; Source 2 (Set 1): AUD (shnid=91977) Taper(s): David Barfield and or David Lane; Source: (OTS)… [1]. Also: Uploader re-released the matrix, claiming it represents a serious improvement over the first version [1]
- **gd1987-09-19.126284.mtx.eichorn.sbeok.t-flac16**: transferred by Roger Eichorn; source: Matrix from Source 1: SBD (shnid=76469) SBD>CD>EAC>FLAC; Source 2 (Set 1): AUD (shnid=91977) Taper(s): David Barfield and/or David Lane Source: (OTS) Nakamichi… [2]. Also: Uploader admits the release was a huge embarrassing gaffe and redid the matrix on December 16, 2013 [31]
- **gd1987-09-19.137413.sbd.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X90) [6]. Also: Uploader used two sets of masters to make the show complete, with help from Joe B. Jones [6]
- **gd1987-09-19.sbd.painoman.76469.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Painoman and Jay Serafin; source: SBD>TAMH*>CD>EAC>FLAC (Most likely SBD>PCM>DAT>CD>EAC>FLAC) [8]. Also: Original CDs were provided by Jay Serafin in 2000, with extraction by PainoMan in 2006 [8]
- **gd1987-09-19.176816.senn441.lamarre.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Doug Lamarre; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Doug Lamarre's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 441 mics > Sony D5M [11]. Also: M. Laurentis provided an AT835B source supplying a 0:17 patch in Space [11]
- **gd1987-09-19.nak300.pasternak.mallick.105569.flac16**: taped by Jon Pasternak; transferred by Jon Pasternak and Dave Mallick; source: Nakamichi CM300's/CP4's>Marantz PMD-420>Cass(m), [14]
- **gd1987-09-19.nak300.damico.90485.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Joe D'Amico; transferred by Joe D'Amico; source: nak 300 mics w/ cp4 shotguns > sony d-5 D [15]
- **gd1987-09-19.nakcm304.suraci.82419.flac16**: taped by Tony Suraci; transferred by Tony Suraci; source: Nak CM304's>Sony D5M [18]

claims.text: Listener attended their second show, noting the Farm Aid comments were strange at the time
Listener describes Crazy Fingers, Uncle John's, and Playin' In The Band as real sweet
Listener rates the sound as high quality grade A with a perfect mix of crowd and music
Listener notes Maggie's Farm rocks, but wished for the other song after it per Bob's direction
Listener rates the sound quality at 4 out of 5 stars
Listener recalls bringing their mother and father to this specific show
Listener considers the Playing in the Band performance an overlooked gem
Listener notes very good recording quality with extremely minor distortion present
Listener notes Dead Heads in 1987 disliked Black Peter and Around & Around as downers
Listener states Miracle, Maggie's Farm, and Black Peter were part of the Farm Aid III TV broadcast
Listener calls High Time real sweet and a highlight, noting an interesting slide solo from Bob
Listener compares the show to the previous night's monster Dew, calling this one outstanding playing
Listener notes lots of bandwidth retained and bright levels, hearing the Garden in its resonant glory
Listener describes the venue as filled with the same energy as the night before
Uploader admits the release was a huge embarrassing gaffe and redid the matrix on December 16, 2013
Uploader re-released the matrix, claiming it represents a serious improvement over the first version
Uploader notes Maggie's Farm was broadcast on TV for Farm Aid
Uploader used two sets of masters to make the show complete, with help from Joe B. Jones
Original CDs were provided by Jay Serafin in 2000, with extraction by PainoMan in 2006
Doug Lamarre provided the master cassette, and Charlie Miller handled the transfer and coordination
M. Laurentis provided an AT835B source supplying a 0:17 patch in Space
